chunks: From him, from al-Barqī, from Ibn Sinān, from Ḥudhayfah ibn Manṣūr, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: There is something people say: “The ʿawrah of the believer is forbidden to the believer.”

So he said: “It is not as they take it. Rather, what is meant by the ʿawrah of the believer is that he slips in a misstep or speaks of something for which he may be blamed, and then someone preserves it against him in order to shame him with it one day.”

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believer whose dignity and faults are to be protected
key_terms.عَوْرَةُ: the vulnerable or shameful matter of a person that must not be exposed
key_terms.فَيَحْفَظَ: to retain and keep track of something
key_terms.لِيُعَيِّرَ: to shame or reproach someone with it
key_terms.يَزِلَّ: to slip into an error or lapse

ai.seo_question: What does “the ʿawrah of the believer is forbidden to the believer” mean in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the prohibited “ʿawrah” of a believer is not merely physical exposure, but also a believer’s moral lapse or blameworthy statement that another person keeps in order to disgrace him later. It teaches the sanctity of a believer’s dignity and condemns storing up another’s faults for future reproach.
